title: Jacket Potato with Chilli con Carne
subtitle: Baked potato with beef and kidney bean chilli and soured cream
excerpt: Jacket potato with chilli con carne is a baked potato split and topped with a rich beef and kidney bean chilli, finished with soured cream and grated cheddar. It is one of the great British weeknight or weekend lunch combinations: filling, flexible, and made from ingredients kept in the storecupboard.
sourceNotes: Jacket potato with chilli is a British dinner and lunch combination that became widely popular in the 1980s and 1990s in pubs, cafeterias, and home cooking. The chilli is a simplified version of the Tex-Mex dish adapted for British home cooking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the chilli con carne separately in portions for up to 3 months. Bake the potatoes fresh.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a double batch of the chilli and freeze in portions.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The chilli improves if made a day ahead.

content.text: Jacket potato with chilli needs two things done well: the potato must be completely soft inside with a crisp, salted skin, and the chilli must be thick enough to sit on top rather than flooding the potato. Both are straightforward. Start the potato first as it takes 1 to 1.5 hours in the oven.

Preheat the oven to 200C. Rub the {{potatoes-floury}} baking potatoes all over with {{olive-oil}} of olive oil and season with {{salt-table}} of salt. Pierce each potato several times with a fork. Place directly on the oven rack and bake for 1 to 1.25 hours until the skin is completely crisp and a skewer meets no resistance anywhere inside.

Heat {{olive-oil}} of olive oil in a large saucepan over a medium-high heat. Add {{onion}} onion and {{pepper-red}} pepper. Cook for 5 minutes until soft. Add {{garlic}} garlic and cook for 1 minute more.

Add {{beef-mince}} of beef mince and brown well, breaking up any lumps. Drain off excess fat. Stir in {{chilli-powder}} of chilli powder, {{cumin-ground}} of ground cumin, {{smoked-paprika}} of smoked paprika, and {{tomato-puree}} of tomato puree. Cook for 1 minute.
Add {{tinned-tomatoes}} tinned tomatoes and {{kidney-beans}} kidney beans. Season with {{salt-table}} salt. Simmer for 30 minutes until thickened and rich. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

Score a cross in the top of each potato and squeeze the sides to open it. Spoon {{beef-mince}} the chilli con carne generously on top. Add a spoonful of {{soured-cream}} soured cream and scatter {{cheddar}} grated cheddar over. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: The potato skin is soft rather than crisp
items.cause: The potato was not baked directly on the oven rack, or was wrapped in foil.
items.fix: Place potatoes directly on the oven rack, never on a tray or in foil. Foil traps steam and produces soft skin. Rub well with oil and salt before baking.

content.text: Jacket potato with chilli is a classic of 1980s British casual food. It appeared on pub menus, in works canteens, at bonfire nights, and in school lunch halls across the country. The baked potato has been a British staple since the nineteenth century. The chilli topping reflects the influence of American Tex-Mex cooking, which became popular in Britain from the 1970s onward. It remains one of the most popular lunch and dinner choices on the British high street.
